plan.planning_summary: This control axis tests whether a 22-layer alternating ZnS/Al2O3 stack on CaF2 substrate can achieve dual-band transmission at 3.25-3.35 μm and 4.20-4.30 μm while suppressing 2.50-3.10 μm and 4.45-5.00 μm. The design draws from recalled knowledge of mid-IR dielectric coating practice: ZnS provides high index (~2.2-2.4 in mid-IR), Al2O3 provides lower index (~1.6-1.7), and quarter-wave-like stacks create interference-based bandpass behavior. I would have wanted to look up exact n/k dispersion data for both materials across 2.5-5.0 μm, verify CaF2 substrate transmission in this range, and confirm deposition stress compatibility for 22-layer stacks.

routes.title: 22-layer ZnS/Al2O3 alternating stack with independent thickness optimization on CaF2
routes.scientific_hypothesis: An alternating high/low index dielectric stack with 22 layers can produce two distinct transmission windows at 3.25-3.35 μm and 4.20-4.30 μm through constructive interference, while adjacent bands experience destructive interference and suppression.
routes.design_principle: Quarter-wave stack theory: alternating layers with optical thickness near λ/4 create high reflectance stopbands. By deviating from strict quarter-wave thicknesses and optimizing individually, multiple passbands can emerge at specific wavelengths where phase conditions allow transmission. The index contrast between ZnS and Al2O3 provides sufficient reflectance per interface to build effective stopbands with ~11 layer pairs.
soft_objectives: Maximize mean transmittance in 3.25-3.35 μm band
Maximize mean transmittance in 4.20-4.30 μm band
Minimize mean transmittance in 2.50-3.10 μm band
Minimize mean transmittance in 4.45-5.00 μm band
manufacturing_considerations: 22 layers is within stated limit of 24
ZnS and Al2O3 are conventional evaporatable/sputterable IR dielectrics
Total thickness ~15-20 μm may require stress management
theory_basis: Recalled: ZnS has refractive index ~2.2-2.4 in 3-5 μm range with low extinction
Recalled: Al2O3 has refractive index ~1.6-1.7 in mid-IR with good transparency
Recalled: Quarter-wave stacks produce stopbands centered at design wavelength
Recalled: Deviating from quarter-wave thickness can create multiple passbands
Recalled: CaF2 (Daimon-20 dataset) is transparent in 2.5-5.0 μm range and commonly used as IR substrate
expected_advantages: High index contrast (~0.5-0.7) provides strong interference effects per layer pair
22 layers gives ~11 pairs, sufficient for deep stopbands
Independent thickness optimization allows tuning for dual-band requirement
All materials are conventional IR coating materials
known_risks: Uncertain: Exact n/k dispersion of ZnS and Al2O3 across 2.5-5.0 μm - need registry data to confirm
Uncertain: Whether Al2O3 has absorption features in 4-5 μm range that would limit performance
Uncertain: Daimon-20 CaF2 substrate refractive index at these wavelengths affects matching
Uncertain: Whether 22 layers is optimal or if fewer layers could achieve similar performance
Uncertain: Deposition stress and adhesion for thick multi-layer stacks not verified
What would settle: Measured dispersion data from registry, stress measurements from deposition trials
routes.execution_request_english: Optimize a 22-layer planar multilayer coating on CaF2 (Daimon-20) substrate with air incidence. Stack sequence: ZnS, Al2O3 (Kischkat), ZnS, Al2O3 (Kischkat), ZnS, Al2O3 (Kischkat), ZnS, Al2O3 (Kischkat), ZnS, Al2O3 (Kischkat), ZnS, Al2O3 (Kischkat), ZnS, Al2O3 (Kischkat), ZnS, Al2O3 (Kischkat), ZnS, Al2O3 (Kischkat), ZnS, Al2O3 (Kischkat), ZnS, Al2O3 (Kischkat) (22 coating layers total). Optimize all 22 layer thicknesses independently with bounds ±25 nm around baseline [911.21, 804.98, 703.61, 672.14, 356.02, 1229.24, 356.71, 570.30, 870.84, 635.33, 370.60, 1162.40, 332.44, 462.47, 857.27, 417.97, 831.12, 1275.13, 925.63, 416.00, 805.81, 889.71] nm. Target: maximize transmittance in 3250-3350 nm and 4200-4300 nm bands, minimize transmittance in 2500-3100 nm and 4450-5000 nm bands. Use coherent transfer matrix method. Materials: zns, Al2O3 (Kischkat), substrate CaF2 (Daimon-20). No metal layers. Layer count fixed at 22.
routes.revision_reason: Continuation from iteration_19: Relax thickness optimization bounds from ±15 nm to ±25 nm around best candidate from round 4 (thicknesses: [911.21, 804.98, 703.61, 672.14, 356.02, 1229.24, 356.71, 570.30, 870.84, 635.33, 370.60, 1162.40, 332.44, 462.47, 857.27, 417.97, 831.12, 1275.13, 925.63, 416.00, 805.81, 889.71] nm). This widens phase-tuning bandwidth while anchoring near proven geometry. Repaired material name from CaF2 to Daimon-20 per registry resolution requirement.

selector_prompt.system:
You are the internal material-dataset selector inside a scientific TMM
harness. This is not route planning and you must not redesign the route.
Return exactly one JSON object and no markdown:
{"selections":[{"request_id":"material_01","selected_rank":1,"provider":"rii_sqlite","dataset_id":562,"reason":"..."}]}

The user question is authoritative. Each request contains candidates already
retrieved from the local MaterialRegistry and sorted by three equal physical
metrics: target-band coverage, n/k completeness, and sampling density. Rank 1
is the most physically reliable candidate; lower rank means less reliable.
Choose exactly one candidate from the supplied list for every request. Never
invent, rename, or edit a provider or dataset_id. The selected_rank must point
to the selected array element, and provider/dataset_id must copy that element.

Material identity, stoichiometry, explicit material state/preparation, and an
explicit requested source are hard constraints. A candidate with
formula_exact=false or semantic_match=same_element_family is not an allowed
substitute for a formula request. SiO is not SiO2, even if the SiO2 candidate
has better physical coverage. When several candidates satisfy the hard
constraints, select the highest-ranked one (usually rank 1). If no candidate
satisfies them, return selected_rank:null, provider:null, dataset_id:null and
reason:"needs_confirmation" for that request.
